fact: The EDPA, with an Acting Chief Executive Officer, is running an outreach campaign with information desks in major towns and says it has a five-year strategy.

The EDPA reports its survey found about 80% of Trade Fair stand visitors not adequately aware of the Data Protection Act and 55.2% of the public finding the Authority difficult to access, and is setting up information desks in major towns covering registration requirements (date is the article's publication date).

The article says the Data Protection Act, 2022 regulates the collection, processing, disclosure and protection of personal data and is relevant to publishing personal information online (date is the article's publication date).
The Ministry of ICT stated that oversight of Data Protection Act 2022 compliance is vested in ESCCOM as the statutory authority (date is the article's publication date).
The Ministry of ICT referred to implementation and enforcement of the Data Protection Act 2022 as current (date is the article's publication date).

ESCCOM, acting as the EDPA under the Data Protection Act No. 5 of 2022, has powers to investigate breaches, resolve complaints and impose sanctions, and runs a website, email and phone complaint channel.
The Act binds public and private bodies including ministries, with a 72-hour mandatory breach notification to the EDPA, per ESCCOM's Acting CEO.

The EDPA opened a formal investigation into the Ministry of Home Affairs and wrote to it over unblurred national identity documents posted online; the Ministry had not notified the EDPA, and no outcome was reported (date is the article's publication date).
The EDPA launched its 2026 awareness campaign 'Take Control of Your Data' and has a registration regime for organisations.
The article says the Act was enacted in 2022, that organisations may not collect personal data unless registered with the authority, and that the compliance deadline was 31 March 2026.

The EDPA ran an awareness campaign setting out eight data subject rights, and organisations were conducting data mapping ahead of the 31 March 2026 compliance deadline (date is the article's publication date).

The World Bank's Eswatini Economic Update recommends fully operationalizing the Cybersecurity Agency and the Data Protection Office through a national change management programme; the page gives no date for the statement, so its published date is used.

fact: The Eswatini Data Protection Authority lists an enforcement notice under section 41 of the Data Protection Act 2022 issued to the Royal Science Technology Park (RSTP) in March 2025.
The Authority lists enforcement notices under section 41 of the Act issued in June 2024 to MTN Eswatini and to Liberty Life Swaziland Limited.
The Authority's dated enforcement notices under section 41 of the Act, the latest in March 2025, show the Act in operation.
The Eswatini Data Protection Authority, operating its own site, issued enforcement notices under the Act in June 2024 and March 2025.
The Data Protection Act, 2022 (Act No. 5 of 2022) was assented by King Mswati III and gazetted on 4 March 2022; the page states no commencement date.
